Order No.06/Dated- 15.05.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Pakur (Mufassil) P.S. Case No. 31 of 2022 corresponding to G.R. No.259 of 2022 registered under Sections 498A, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, pending in the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate Pakur, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per F.I.R., the allegation made against the petitioner is that informant was married to petitioner according to muslim rites and custom and initially lived peacefully.
After giving birth to their first child, informant faced demands from her husband (the petitioner) and her in-laws for money for doing business.
Upon refusing, she was tortured and eventually ousted from her matrimonial home following her husband's second marriage and further demands for Rs.1,00,000/-.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that in compliance of notice issued under Section 41A of Cr.P.C., he has appeared before the Investigating Officer and after taking his statement, he has been released on bond with undertaking to further cooperate in the investigation of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to him.

Hence, the petitioner may be extended Wasikul @ Asikul Shekh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53895400/
1 the privilege of anticipatory bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel appearing for opposite party No.2 has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submitted that there are serious allegation against the petitioner about mental and physical torture to the informant and he has also not paid the maintenance amount awarded by the Family Court which is lying dues to the tune of more than Rs.3 Lakhs and distress warrant was also issued against the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may not be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case particularly in view of the fact that petitioner is cooperating in the investigation and has been released on bond by the police with undertaking to cooperate in further investigation.

Therefore, without expressing any view on merits, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of as there is no apprehension of arrest of the petitioner and charge-sheet has also been submitted, therefore, petitioner is directed to appear before the learned Court below and seek regular bail which shall be disposed of on the same day in strict compliance of guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2021(10) SCC 773 as well as recent observation of Hon'ble Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2023- SCC online (SC) 452 & 2023- Live Law (SC) 233.
(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sachin Wasikul @ Asikul Shekh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53895400/
